title: Practice Set SLJ4 — Picking the Partition Column
description: Junior storage layout recognition track. Module 4 of 5 — picking the partition column.

datasets.description: Schema reference (sample rows). NordGrid Energy at junior scale; the CSV is a small sample for schema reference.

tasks.title: partitionBy('meter_id') Was Wrong

description.context: Partition-column selection has rules. The cardinality (number of distinct values) of the partition column directly becomes the number of directories on disk. A column like meter_id has 500K distinct values — partitioning by it creates 500K directories, each holding one or two rows. This is the small-file problem multiplied by 1000. The general rule: partition columns should have BETWEEN ~10 and ~10,000 distinct values for production datasets. Below that, you don't get enough pruning; above that, you trigger the small-file disaster.
description.task: What is wrong, and what is the rule?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Code: meters.write.partitionBy('meter_id').parquet('layout/')

Distinct Meter Ids: 500000

Directories Created: 500000

Average Rows Per Partition: 1 (one row per meter)

Average File Size Per Partition: 300 bytes

Write Time: 47 minutes for 500K-row dataset (vs 8 seconds with date partitioning)

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: Layout where meter_id (500K distinct values) was used as partition column, creating 500K directories

evidence.label: Plan output
evidence.content:
$ ls layout/ | head -5
  meter_id=ABC0000001/
  meter_id=ABC0000002/
  meter_id=ABC0000003/
  meter_id=ABC0000004/
  meter_id=ABC0000005/
  ... (500,000 directories total)

$ ls layout/meter_id=ABC0000001/
  part-00000.parquet  (304 bytes)

# Query: filter(col('region') == 'NORTH').count()
+- FileScan parquet [meter_id, daily_kw, region, customer_type]
   PartitionFilters: []                  ← region not partitioned
   PushedFilters: [EqualTo(region, NORTH)]
   PartitionCount: 500000                ← reads ALL 500K directories
   Files read: 500000 (304 bytes each)
   Total bytes read: 152 MB
   Total query time: 22 minutes

fields.label: What is wrong, and what is the rule?
options: Partitioning works correctly; the slow query time is expected for 500K-row datasets. Rule: keep dataset sizes below 100K rows OR partition by a high-cardinality column to spread work.

meter_id has 500K distinct values; using it as partition column creates 500K directories with one row each. Per-directory overhead × 500K destroys performance. Rule: 10-10,000 distinct values, not 500K.
The 500K directories are correct; the query is the bug. Rewrite as filter(col('meter_id').isin([...])) to enable pruning across the meter_id partition column for region-filtered queries.
meter_id is a string column; partitioning by string columns is forbidden because Spark cannot type the directory names properly. Rule: only partition by numeric or date columns.
fields.correctAnswer: meter_id has 500K distinct values; using it as partition column creates 500K directories with one row each. Per-directory overhead × 500K destroys performance. Rule: 10-10,000 distinct values, not 500K.
fields.rationale: Cardinality is the load-bearing rule.partitionBy(col) creates one directory per unique value.
fields.distractorRationale: Option A: Treats large datasets as needing more partitions; the relationship inverts at high cardinality.

tasks.pssReference: PSI2 lesson 5 (Partition Column Selection — cardinality rules).

tasks.title: Date + Region — The Canonical Pattern

description.context: After learning what NOT to do (high cardinality, single column, hourly), the canonical good pattern emerges: date + region. partitionBy('date', 'region') uses TWO partition columns. Spark creates a nested directory structure: date=*/region=*/. The combined cardinality is manageable (365 days × 4 regions = 1460 directories per year), and the two columns match how queries actually filter — most NordGrid queries are 'a time range AND a region'. Either filter alone prunes substantially; both together prune almost everything except the slice the query needs.
description.task: Why does this pattern work well for NordGrid's typical queries?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Code: meters.write.partitionBy('date', 'region').parquet('layout/')

Date Range: 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31 (365 days)

Regions: [NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, WEST]

Total Partitions: 1460 (365 × 4)

Average Partition Size: 180MB

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: Layout with partitionBy('date', 'region') showing the canonical two-column pattern at NordGrid scale

evidence.label: Plan output
evidence.content:
$ ls -R layout/
layout/date=2025-04-30/region=NORTH/
  part-00000.parquet  (~180 MB)
layout/date=2025-04-30/region=SOUTH/
  part-00000.parquet  (~180 MB)
... (similar for EAST, WEST)

# Query A: filter(col('date') == '2025-04-30').count()
   PartitionFilters: [(date = 2025-04-30)]
   PartitionCount: 4         ← read 4 directories (all regions for that date)

# Query B: filter((date == '2025-04-30') & (region == 'NORTH')).count()
   PartitionFilters: [(date = 2025-04-30), (region = NORTH)]
   PartitionCount: 1         ← read 1 directory only

# Query C: filter(col('region') == 'NORTH').count()
   PartitionFilters: [(region = NORTH)]
   PartitionCount: 365       ← read 365 directories (all dates for NORTH)

fields.label: Why does this pattern work well for NordGrid's typical queries?
options: The two-column nested layout supports three access patterns. Time-range queries get 4 partitions. Point queries get 1 partition. Full-region scans get 365 partitions. Either filter alone prunes substantially.

Two-column partitioning is purely cosmetic — internally Spark treats it identically to no partitioning. The PartitionCount values shown are misleading; actual scan times are similar across all three queries shown above.

This pattern works because date is FIRST in partitionBy(); reversing the order to partitionBy('region', 'date') would prevent pruning entirely. The first partition column has special pruning privileges.
1460 partitions is too many; this layout suffers from the small-file problem covered in SLJ3.1. Switch to date-only partitioning (365 directories) to fix the per-directory overhead issue.
fields.correctAnswer: The two-column nested layout supports three access patterns. Time-range queries get 4 partitions. Point queries get 1 partition. Full-region scans get 365 partitions. Either filter alone prunes substantially.
fields.rationale: The date+region pattern aligns with NordGrid's actual query mix.Time-range queries (daily reports) prune on date.
fields.distractorRationale:
Option B: Treats partitioning as cosmetic; PartitionCount drives actual read scope.
Option C: Invents an order-of-columns rule.

tasks.pssReference: PSI2 lesson 5 (Partition Column Selection — multi-column patterns).
